subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce for protected config writes initiated from agent-visible errors, host exec, plugin cron hooks, and the `openclaw config patch` CLI?
rationale: The right fix changes security posture and persisted config authority, and current source proves partial guardrails but not the exact auto-writer described by the reporter.

options.title: Guard protected config mutations
options.body: Remove or split model-visible protected config assignments and require explicit operator provenance or approval for CLI/plugin/cron writes to exec and sandbox settings.

options.title: Keep CLI as operator-trusted
options.body: Document that host exec can run the CLI as an operator-equivalent path and limit this issue to removing unsafe agent-visible error text.

options.title: Pause for full incident repro
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers can reproduce the exact memory-core/error-message auto-patcher before choosing the boundary change.

recommendation.title: Guard protected config mutations
recommendation.body: Remove or split model-visible protected config assignments and require explicit operator provenance or approval for CLI/plugin/cron writes to exec and sandbox settings.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged gateway config guard work is the closest current boundary implementation for protected config writes.
